text:
devon: Quick brain-dump — I'm worried our current iterator resume + retry model is leaky across SDKs. Sketching a minimal handshake that keeps transports thin.

devon: Problem: when a client iterates a paged stream and a retry occurs we either re-request from the beginning (wasteful) or require SDK-level cursor replay logic. Both are awkward across HTTP/gRPC and language runtimes.

maria: yep. we saw this in the metrics team — huge duplicate token counts when a page request retries mid-emit. :grimacing:

lee: can you sketch the handshake? curious how heavy it is on the transport.

devon: idea: server issues opaque resume tokens and also accepts a short "retry window" header that means "requests within X ms can be de-duped server-side if they look like retransmits of the same cursor". SDKs just surface two fields: resume_token (string) and retry_window_ms (int). Transport sends them as headers.

devon: proto example (HTTP-centric, but trivial to map to gRPC metadata):

```
GET /v1/objects?page_cursor=abc
X-Resume-Token: "r:W2..."
X-Retry-Window: 2000   # ms
```

server behavior: if request arrives with same page_cursor + resume token and within window, server will return cached page response or a short 204+retry-indicator. If outside window treat as normal new request.

yael: love the simplicity. This avoids SDKs having to rehydrate iterators and buffers on retry. Two questions: 1) how do we handle partial-page emits (streamed tokens) vs batch pages? 2) what's the semantics for idempotent writes in this model?

devon: for streamed tokens we attach the resume token to the last acknowledged frame. If a client reconnects mid-stream it sends the token and server resumes from next item. For batch pages it's the same — token marks page boundary.

ashley: concern: many languages have GC/timer differences — relying on ms windows could be racy. Also, opaque tokens must be compact and stable across model variants.

maria: tradeoff: shorter window -> fewer accidental dedups, more client retries hitting the server; longer -> increased chance of accidentally deduping distinct retries. We can make the default conservative (2s) and expose override per-iterator.

lee: mapping to gRPC: use metadata keys `x-resume-token` and `x-retry-window-ms`. Works fine for unary and streaming. For bidi streams we include token in OpenStream, then use per-frame ack metadata when feasible.

devon: edge cases: multi-transport proxies (load balancers) dropping custom headers. Action: add an ID in query param fallback `resume_token=...` as optional.

yael: what about auth? resume tokens should be bound to the same auth context to avoid token replay across users.

devon: yes token encoding will include hashed principal + TTL. Server validates principal match.

ashley: sounds good. From SDK surface POV: propose 2 API options for each language: (A) zero-config behavior where iterator automatically sends headers if server returns token in response; (B) explicit control via IteratorResumeOptions { enabled: bool, retryWindowMs?: number, resumeToken?: string }.

maria: prefer explicit opt-in for initial rollout (so we can measure token issuance/dup). Feature flag via console + SDK default off.

devon: plan: server-side RFC to add headers + query fallback, implement on staging; lang SDKs add IteratorResumeOptions and pass headers when present + expose token getter. Rollout: opt-in for 2 weeks, then default on if metrics ok.

ashley: action items:
- devon: server RFC and staging PR for header support — due EOW.
- yael: draft token encoding spec + principal-binding — due Tue.
- lee: add gRPC metadata mapping for Go/TS — quick PR.
- maria: telemetry hooks to flag duplicate-token incidents + token issuance count.

infra-bot: deploy-check — found no conflicting header names; recommend `x-rw-resume-token` and `x-rw-retry-window-ms` to avoid collisions.

devon: good call, use `x-rw-...`.

maria: one last note — update docs with example for Python/TS/Go. Make example minimal so product teams can opt in.

lee: i'll add prototype in go-sdk next sprint.

devon: ok closing loop here; i'll open the thread RFC with the header names and sketch code for py/ts/go examples. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
